line: Crowley on Atu XIX: the Sun charged with a rose, Heru-ra-ha the Lord of the New Aeon, and the Rose and Cross (pdf p105, p106).

sections.title: The Sun charged with a rose
sections.line: Crowley's heraldic description of the card and his naming of Heru-ra-ha, the Lord of the New Aeon (pdf p105).

quotes.quote: This card represents, in heraldic language, “the Sun, charged with a rose, on a mount vert
it represents Heru‐ra‐ha, the Lord of the New Aeon, in his manifestation to the race of men as the Sun spiritual, moral, and physical.

sections.title: The rose and the Rose and Cross
sections.line: Crowley on the rose as the flowering of the solar influence (pdf p105) and on the broadening of the idea of the Rose and Cross (pdf p106).

quotes.quote: The rose represents the flowering of the solar influence.
The card itself symbolizes this broadening of the idea of the Rose and Cross.

sections.title: The Paths and the letters
